examples.en: The factory runs its machines every morning.
They started running the new power plant yesterday.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 난방 시설을 가동하는 시간이 길어요.
examples.en: In winter, the heating system runs for a longer time.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 배수 펌프를 가동할 거예요.
examples.en: If it rains a lot, they'll turn on the drainage pump.

examples.ko: 컴퓨터 서버를 하루 종일 가동하고 있어요.
examples.en: We keep the computer server running all day.

examples.ko: 비상 상황에는 이 장치를 바로 가동해야 해요.
examples.en: In an emergency, you have to start this device right away.

explain: 큰 기계나 설비, 시스템을 움직이게 하거나 계속 돌릴 때 써요. 집에서 쓰는 가전은 '켜다'나 '틀다'가 자연스러워요. 반대는 '중단하다'나 '멈추다'예요.
explain_en: Used for starting or keeping large machines, facilities or systems running. For home appliances, 켜다 or 틀다 sounds more natural. The opposite is 중단하다 or 멈추다.

dis.h: start up and run machinery or a factory

p.n: 작동하다 does not take 'machine' as an object.

examples.en: Exercise reduces stress.
The company is trying to reduce costs.

examples.ko: 이 약은 통증을 감소시킬 수 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine can reduce pain.
I'm looking for ways to cut down on trash.
The new system greatly reduced accidents.
After reducing the noise, it became much quieter.

explain: '줄이다'와 같지만, 줄어드는 대상이 양·수치·비율처럼 측정되는 것일 때 글이나 보고서에서 많이 써요. 스스로 줄어들면 '감소하다'이고, 누군가가 줄게 만들면 '감소시키다'예요. 말할 때는 '줄이다'가 훨씬 흔해요.
explain_en: Same idea as '줄이다', but typical in reports and writing when the thing reduced is a measurable amount or rate. '감소하다' is when something decreases by itself; '감소시키다' is when someone makes it decrease. In speech, '줄이다' is far more common.

dis.h: formal; make amounts or levels drop

p.n: 줄이다 is everyday speech; 감소시키다 is more formal or technical.

examples.en: Please don't think of the two matters as linked.
Why do you tie every problem to age?

examples.ko: 그는 성공을 운과 결부시키는 걸 싫어해요.
examples.en: He dislikes attributing success to luck.

examples.ko: 그 일을 제 실수와 결부시킬 필요는 없어요.
examples.en: There's no need to link that matter to my mistake.

examples.ko: 성적을 용돈과 결부시켰더니 아이가 열심히 공부했어요.
examples.en: After I tied grades to allowance, the child studied hard.
If you force a link between the incidents, misunderstandings arise.

explain: 'A를 B와 결부시키다'처럼 말하는 사람이 둘을 엮어서 본다는 뜻이에요. '결부시키지 마세요'나 '억지로 결부시키다'처럼 쓰면 무리하게 엮는다는 느낌이 있어요. 스스로 연결되어 있는 경우는 '결부되다'를 써요.
explain_en: It means the speaker ties two things together, as in 'A를 B와 결부시키다'. In phrases like '결부시키지 마세요' or '억지로 결부시키다' it carries a sense of forcing a link. When the link exists on its own, use '결부되다'.

dis.h: formal: tie A firmly to B

p.n: 연관시키다 is plainer and less formal.

examples.ko: 이 마을 사람들은 대부분 쌀 경작으로 먹고살아요.
examples.en: Most people in this village make a living from rice cultivation.
The cultivated area is shrinking every year.
Cultivation is not easy on a mountain slope.
Grandfather hurt his back from long years of farming.
Farmland is disappearing little by little near the city.

examples.ko: 경작에 쓰는 땅은 비가 충분히 와야 좋아요.
examples.en: Land used for cultivation needs enough rain to be good.

explain: 일상에서는 '농사'라고 많이 말하고, 경작은 뉴스나 설명문에서 땅을 일구는 일을 말할 때 나와요. '경작지', '경작 면적'처럼 땅과 함께 쓰는 말이 많아요. '농사'가 일 전체라면 경작은 땅에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: In daily talk people say '농사' (farming), while 경작 appears in news and written explanations about working the land. It often forms words tied to land, like '경작지' and '경작 면적'. '농사' is the whole job, while 경작 focuses on the land.

examples.ko: 선생님은 새 단어를 일상생활과 관련시켜 가르쳐 주세요.
examples.en: The teacher teaches new words by relating them to daily life.

examples.ko: 이 사건을 그 사람과 관련시키지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't connect this incident to that person.
I thought about the two things together.
If you link a memory to a place, it lasts longer.

examples.ko: 저는 그 일을 제 문제와 관련시켰어요.
examples.en: I connected that matter to my own problem.
The news is linking the two incidents.

explain: '관련되다'는 저절로 연결된 상태이고, '관련시키다'는 누군가 일부러 연결한다는 차이가 있어요. '연결하다'는 물건이나 선에도 쓰지만 '관련시키다'는 일이나 생각을 이을 때 써요. '~을 ~와 관련시키다' 틀로 써요.
explain_en: '관련되다' is a state of being linked on its own, while '관련시키다' means someone links things on purpose. '연결하다' also works for objects and lines, but '관련시키다' is used for events and ideas. The pattern is '~을 ~와 관련시키다'.

p.n: Nearly the same; 관련짓다 stresses seeing a link in the mind.

examples.en: The baby lies there wiggling its fingers.

examples.ko: 아이는 방 한구석에서 꼼지락꼼지락 뭔가를 만들었어요.
examples.en: The child was making something slowly in a corner of the room.
I watched TV, wiggling my toes.

examples.ko: 새끼 고양이가 담요 속에서 꼼지락꼼지락 기어 나왔어요.
examples.en: The kitten wriggled its way out of the blanket.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 하루 종일 꼼지락꼼지락 화분을 손질하세요.
examples.en: Grandpa spends all day slowly tending to his flower pots.

examples.ko: 동생이 꼼지락꼼지락 딴짓만 해서 숙제를 못 끝냈어요.
examples.en: My sibling kept fiddling around and couldn't finish the homework.

explain: '꼼지락거리다'의 부사로, 손가락·발가락처럼 몸의 일부가 느리고 조금씩 움직이는 모습이에요. 작은 동물이나 벌레가 기어가는 느낌은 '꼬물꼬물'이 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is the adverb of '꼼지락거리다', describing a part of the body such as fingers or toes moving slowly and slightly. For the feel of a small animal or bug crawling, '꼬물꼬물' fits better.

examples.ko: 엘리베이터가 사람으로 꽉 차서 꼼짝달싹 못 했어요.
examples.en: The elevator was packed, so I couldn't move an inch.

examples.ko: 폭설 때문에 도로의 차들이 꼼짝달싹 못 해요.
examples.en: Because of the heavy snow, the cars on the road can't budge.

examples.ko: 감기가 심해서 하루 종일 꼼짝달싹 안 하고 누워 있었어요.
examples.en: I had a bad cold, so I lay there all day without moving.

examples.ko: 허리를 다쳐서 꼼짝달싹 할 수가 없어요.
examples.en: I hurt my back and can't move at all.
Mom is watching me, so I can't make a single move.

examples.ko: 너무 무서워서 그 자리에서 꼼짝달싹 못 하고 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I was so scared that I stood there frozen, unable to move.

explain: '꼼짝'을 더 세게 말한 형태로, '꼼짝달싹 못 하다'처럼 거의 굳어진 표현으로 써요. 짧게 '꼼짝 못 하다'라고도 해요. '아내에게 꼼짝 못 하다'처럼 사람 뒤에 '에게'를 붙이면 상대에게 눌려 지낸다는 뜻이 돼요.
explain_en: It is a stronger version of '꼼짝' and is used almost as a fixed expression, '꼼짝달싹 못 하다'. The shorter '꼼짝 못 하다' is also common. With a person plus '에게', as in '아내에게 꼼짝 못 하다', it means being dominated by that person.

examples.en: A knife becomes hard through tempering.

examples.ko: 이번 시즌을 앞두고 선수들이 혹독한 담금질에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: Ahead of this season, the players started harsh, toughening training.

examples.ko: 어려운 시기가 오히려 저에게 담금질이 됐어요.
examples.en: The hard times actually toughened me up.

examples.ko: 담금질 과정에서 열을 잘 조절해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to control the heat well during the tempering process.
That time was a tempering of my heart.
The coach made the team strong through rigorous training.

explain: 원래는 뜨겁게 달군 쇠를 물에 넣어 단단하게 하는 일인데, 힘든 훈련이나 경험으로 사람을 단련한다는 비유로도 많이 써요. 스포츠 뉴스에서 '담금질에 들어가다'라는 표현을 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: Originally it is the process of heating metal and plunging it into water to harden it, but it is also widely used figuratively for toughening a person through hard training or experience. In sports news you often see the expression '담금질에 들어가다'.

examples.en: The father gave the child a shoulder ride.

examples.ko: 축제에서 아들을 목말 태우고 공연을 봤어요.
examples.en: At the festival I put my son on my shoulders and watched the show.
The child climbed onto Dad's shoulders and loves it.
Maybe the shoulder ride was comfortable, because the child fell asleep right away.
If you give a shoulder ride for long, your neck hurts.
My daughter begged to be carried on my shoulders.

explain: 어른이 아이를 어깨에 올릴 때는 '목말을 태우다', 아이가 올라탈 때는 '목말을 타다'로 짝을 맞춰 써요. 아이 키가 커서 구경하기 좋아지는 장면에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: The adult says '목말을 태우다' (give a shoulder ride) and the child says '목말을 타다' (ride on shoulders). It often appears when a child is lifted to see over a crowd.

examples.ko: 이 공장은 연기 방출을 줄이는 노력을 하고 있어요.
examples.en: This factory is working to reduce smoke emissions.

examples.ko: 난로는 열 방출이 빨라서 방이 금방 따뜻해져요.
examples.en: The heater gives off heat quickly, so the room warms up soon.
The club decided to release the underperforming player.
People evacuated because of a gas release accident.
Sweat helps the body release heat.
Emission standards got stricter, so factories are worried.

explain: 방출은 열·가스·에너지가 밖으로 나가는 일에 쓰고, 스포츠에서는 팀이 선수를 내보내는 일에도 써요. 비슷한 '배출'은 쓰레기·물·가스를 내보낼 때 쓰고, 방출은 열·빛·에너지처럼 퍼져 나가는 것에 어울려요. 뉴스에서 '선수 방출'이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 방출 is heat, gas or energy going out, and in sports it means a team letting a player go. The similar '배출' fits waste, water and gas, while 방출 suits things that spread out like heat, light and energy. '선수 방출' is a common news phrase.

examples.en: You must not burn trash carelessly.
He practiced all night, burning with passion.
I burned the old letters in the yard.
The smell of burning fallen leaves feels like autumn.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 마지막 경기에 모든 힘을 불태워요.
examples.en: That player puts everything into the final game.

examples.ko: 지난 일을 잊으려고 사진들을 불태우고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I wanted to burn the photos to forget the past.

explain: '태우다'보다 활활 다 태워 없애는 느낌이 강해요. 불 자체뿐 아니라 열정, 투지 같은 마음에도 비유로 써요. 저절로 타는 건 '불타다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: He poured all his passion into the stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일에 온 힘과 마음을 다한다는 뜻의 비유예요. 운동, 공연, 공부처럼 노력하는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative way to say someone gives all their energy and heart to something. It is used for effort in sports, performances, studying, and so on.

explain_en: It has a stronger sense of burning something up completely than '태우다'. It is used not only for real fire but also figuratively for feelings like passion and fighting spirit. When something burns on its own, use '불타다'.

examples.en: I cut my long hair off with a snip at the hair salon.
Please snip the string with scissors.
Mom cut up the vegetables with quick chops.
The gardener snipped off the tree branches.
I cut my bangs off too short and I regret it.
I snipped out the paper and made a card.

explain: 가위나 칼로 단번에 베어 자르는 소리나 모양이에요. 한 번 자르면 '싹둑', 여러 번 자르면 '싹둑싹둑'이라고 해요. 같은 느낌인데 더 크고 굵은 것은 '썩둑'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It imitates the sound or look of cutting something in one stroke with scissors or a knife. One cut is '싹둑' and repeated cuts are '싹둑싹둑'. A bigger, thicker version of the same feel is '썩둑'.

examples.ko: 이 정수기는 여과 장치가 세 단계예요.
examples.en: This water purifier has a three-stage filtration system.
After filtration, the water becomes much cleaner.

examples.ko: 여과 필터는 석 달마다 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: You have to replace the filter every three months.

examples.ko: 그는 생각을 여과 없이 말해서 가끔 오해를 받아요.
examples.en: He says what he thinks without any filter, so he is sometimes misunderstood.

examples.ko: 여과가 잘 안 되면 물이 탁해요.
examples.en: If the filtering doesn't work well, the water looks cloudy.

examples.ko: 커피는 여과 방식에 따라 맛이 달라요.
examples.en: Coffee tastes different depending on the filtering method.

explain: 물이나 공기를 거르는 일이지만, 말과 정보를 걸러 낼 때도 비유로 써요. 일상에서는 '거르다'라고 하고, '여과 없이'는 생각이나 말을 그대로 드러낼 때 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 그의 발언이 여과 없이 방송에 나갔어요.
phrases.en: His remarks were aired without any editing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이나 영상을 다듬거나 걸러 내지 않고 그대로 드러낼 때 써요. 좋게도 나쁘게도 쓰지만 뉴스나 글에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when words or footage are shown as they are, without being polished or screened. It can be positive or negative and often appears in news and writing.

explain_en: It refers to filtering water or air, but it is also used figuratively for filtering words and information. In everyday speech people say '거르다', and '여과 없이' is common for showing thoughts or words just as they are.

examples.en: Noise lowers work performance.
They say stress weakens immunity.
A bad posture reduced my concentration.
We are looking for what lowers the quality.

examples.ko: 약이 판단력을 저하시킬 수 있으니 조심하세요.
examples.en: The medicine can impair judgment, so be careful.
Unnecessary features slowed it down, so I deleted them.

explain: 저하시키다는 어떤 원인이 수준이나 능력을 낮출 때 써요. 주어에는 사람보다 '소음, 스트레스, 피로, 나쁜 습관' 같은 원인이 많이 와요. 같은 뜻으로 '떨어뜨리다'는 말하기에 더 편해요.
explain_en: 저하시키다 is used when some cause lowers a level or ability. The subject is more often a cause such as noise, stress, fatigue or a bad habit than a person. 떨어뜨리다 means much the same and is easier to say in speech.

examples.en: The teacher steered the topic in another direction.

examples.ko: 회사는 종이 문서를 전자 문서로 전환시켜요.
examples.en: The company converts paper documents into electronic ones.
I opened the window to change the mood.
They built a device that converts heat into electricity.
If you switch your way of thinking, the problem gets easy to solve.
They plan to shift the market toward online.

explain: '전환하다'와 거의 같아서 보통은 '전환하다'를 더 많이 써요. '전환시키다'는 누군가가 일부러 방향을 돌린다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 화제, 분위기, 방식 같은 말과 함께 써요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '전환하다', which people use more often. '전환시키다' has a stronger sense that someone deliberately turns things around. It goes with words like '화제', '분위기', '방식'.

examples.en: This exercise keeps the effect going for a long time.

examples.ko: 좋은 습관을 지속시키려면 매일 조금씩 하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: To keep a good habit going, it is best to do a little every day.

examples.ko: 회사는 이 서비스를 앞으로도 지속시킬 계획이에요.
examples.en: The company plans to keep this service running in the future too.

examples.ko: 그는 어려운 상황에서도 좋은 성적을 지속시켰어요.
examples.en: He kept his good grades going even in a hard situation.
Keeping people's interest going is the hardest part.
I am sorry I could not keep that enthusiasm going.

explain: '계속하다'는 하던 일을 이어서 하는 것이고, '지속시키다'는 상태나 효과가 끊기지 않게 하는 쪽이에요. 목적어로 '효과, 관계, 관심, 서비스'처럼 상태를 나타내는 말이 와요. 말할 때는 '유지하다'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: '계속하다' means to carry on doing something, while '지속시키다' is about making a state or effect not break off. Its objects are state-like nouns such as '효과', '관계', '관심', '서비스'. In speech, '유지하다' is more common.

dis.h: make an action or process continue over time

p.n: 유지하다 sounds like keeping the effort at the same level rather than continuing it over time.

en: to spin; to turn; to rotate

examples.en: The machine spins its blades quickly.
Try rotating the picture to the right.
I rotated the phone photo by 90 degrees.
When you turn the wheel, the bicycle moves forward.
I turned the chair around and looked toward the window.
Where is the button that rotates the screen?

explain: 무언가를 빙글 돌게 만들 때 써요. 사진이나 화면을 돌리는 컴퓨터 말로도 많이 써요. 일상에서는 '돌리다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. 스스로 도는 것은 '회전하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used for making something spin around, and also as a computer term for rotating a photo or screen. In daily speech 돌리다 sounds far more natural. Something turning on its own is 회전하다.

examples.en: I train my puppy every day.
The coach trained the players hard.
I've been put in charge of training the new hires.
I'm training my child to sleep alone.
Training a horse takes a long time.
We trained the staff and sent them out to the site.

explain: '~을 훈련시키다'는 내가 직접 하지 않고 대상이 훈련하게 만드는 말이에요. 내가 몸으로 연습하면 '훈련하다'예요. 같은 뜻으로 '훈련을 시키다'로 띄어 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: ~을 훈련시키다 means you make someone or something else go through training instead of doing it yourself. If you practice yourself, it is 훈련하다. You can also split it as 훈련을 시키다 with the same meaning.

dis.h: make someone or an animal practice

p.n: 조련 is specifically animal taming/training; 훈련시키다 is general.
